title: fix(components): element:number reads its object from dataSource.object, as the spec binding declares (objectui#10909)
body:
Fixes #10909
Clause-②: yes (widening)

Implemented on branch `claude/issue-10909-element-number-datasource` by the `os-dev` run dispatched from the `domain:ui` seat 2 session `session_014mXUNuFomfj24w7s1pZzhN` (claim comment 5866532141 on the card).

## What changed

- **`ElementNumberRenderer`** (`packages/components/src/renderers/basic/elements.tsx`) now reads the spec's per-element binding (`PageComponentSchema.dataSource`) through `useElementDataSource`, the way its element twin `element:record_picker` does.
  - The object resolves ONCE as `dataSource.object ?? properties.object`, and that one value is the fetch guard, the `adapter.aggregate` / `adapter.find` target and the `useDataInvalidation` key. `dataSource.object` wins when both are set.
  - While a named view is unresolved or unresolvable, there is no object, even beside a flat `properties.object`.
- **Filter (seat ruling B):** with a binding present, `properties.filter` is AND-combined with the binding's filter and with its view's. The lowering and merge are the ones `ElementDataSourceGate` uses (`toFilterNodeSafely` + `mergeFilterNodes`), so neither filter is dropped. A merge the converter refuses shows the configuration-error panel and aggregates nothing. With no binding, `properties.filter` reaches the adapter exactly as authored.
- **Registration:** `element:number` is registered through `elementDataSourceBlock(...)` (from `@object-ui/core`), so `Registry.register` injects the one shared `dataSource` declaration (`ELEMENT_DATA_SOURCE_INPUT`, `binding: 'object'`).
  - `object` is no longer `required: true`.
  - The `object` input's description states its precedence.
  - The `filter` input's description is exactly: "Criteria the aggregate is scoped by. When a node-level `dataSource` binding also supplies a filter (its own, or the saved view its `view` names), the two are AND-combined: neither is dropped."
- **Pins:** new `packages/components/src/renderers/basic/__tests__/elementNumber.dataSourceBinding-10909.test.tsx` (18 rows). It is registered as the `element:number.dataSource` member pin in `apps/console/src/__tests__/registry-inputs-spec-parity.test.ts`, which the parity census requires once the block declares an object-armed input.
- **Docs:** `content/docs/guide/data-source.md` gains the `element:number` row in the per-element binding table. A paragraph says how the two `element:*` rows read the binding, and that they differ on `filter`: `record_picker` substitutes, `element:number` AND-combines.
- **Changeset:** `.changeset/10909-element-number-datasource.md`, `'@object-ui/components': minor`, with `Clause-②: yes (widening)`.

## H1: reproduced on `main` (733fd5ac65)

The probe used the real `SchemaRenderer`, the real registry, and an `AdapterCtx` adapter with `aggregate` / `find` spies. The probe file was temporary and not committed.

```text
H1 dataSource-form :: aggregate calls=[] find calls=[] painted="—"
H1 properties-form :: aggregate calls=["contact"] find calls=[] painted="7"
```

The same probe on this branch:

```text
H1 dataSource-form :: aggregate calls=["contact"] find calls=[] painted="7"
H1 properties-form :: aggregate calls=["contact"] find calls=[] painted="7"
```

## `ElementDataSourceSchema` members: which ones this renderer reads

| member | read? | how |
|---|---|---|
| `object` | yes | `dataSource.object ?? properties.object`. There is no object at all while a named view is unresolved or unresolvable. A binding naming no object (empty or not a string) supplies nothing, and the flat object stands. |
| `view` | yes | Through `useElementDataSource`: the saved view's `filter` scopes the aggregate. While the view resolves, the shared loading panel shows and nothing is read. If it cannot be resolved, the shared error panel (`element-number-datasource-error`) shows and nothing is aggregated. |
| `filter` | yes | `properties.filter` AND (view filter AND binding filter), lowered and merged as `ElementDataSourceGate` does. Neither is dropped; a refused merge reports and aggregates nothing. Context tokens are handled by the existing `useResolvedFilter` on the merged value. There is no record-context binding (objectui#7297 stays on hold), and the filter-shape note (objectui#8945) is untouched. |
| `sort` | no | An aggregate has no ordering. It never reaches `aggregate()` or `find()`, and the whole options bag is asserted. |
| `limit` | no | A capped count would be a wrong number. Neither the binding's nor a view's `pagination.pageSize` reaches `aggregate()` or the `find()` fallback. |
| `columns` / `viewType` (view-only composed keys) | no | A metric has no projection and no view kind. |

No member is declared per member. The only declaration is the injected `dataSource` input (`type: 'object'`, `binding: 'object'`), whose description lists the binding's five members generically. Which of them this block reads is pinned at the read site.

## The registration change: what `elementDataSourceBlock` changes, exactly

`elementDataSourceBlock` is a marker. It adds the renderer to a `WeakSet` and returns it unchanged, so it adds no gate, no loading state and no fetch. The declaration is emitted by `withElementDataSourceInput` inside `Registry.register`. Measured on the live registry:

- the registered inputs on head are `object,aggregate!,field,filter,format,prefix,suffix,dataSource` (`!` = required). On base, `object!` carried the required mark and there was no `dataSource`;
- `validateTree` on `{ type: 'element:number', dataSource: { object: 'contact' }, aggregate: 'count' }` returns no diagnostic. On base it returned `is missing required prop "object"` and `has no prop "dataSource"`.

The render-path changes come from `useElementDataSource` and from the filter merge, and they reach only a node that carries a binding:

- a named `view` reads saved views and shows the shared loading panel while it resolves;
- an unresolvable `view`, or a filter refused in either merge, shows the shared error panel;
- a node with no `dataSource` resolves `absent` synchronously, so the `properties` form issues no new read, shows no new panel, and sends its filter unlowered. This is pinned: the control row asserts `getObjectSchema` is never called.

## Pins: red before, green on head

File: `elementNumber.dataSourceBinding-10909.test.tsx`, 18 rows. The file was byte-identical in all three runs, and each base run used a temporary detached worktree that was removed afterwards.

| run | result |
|---|---|
| head 37bc45f74c | `Tests  18 passed (18)` |
| base 733fd5ac65 | `Tests  16 failed \| 2 passed (18)` — the 2 green rows are the `properties`-form control and the empty-`object` binding row |
| previous head 48d755dfe1 (rule A) | `Tests  6 failed \| 12 passed (18)` |

The 6 rows red on the previous head:

- the two AND rows (binding + properties filter, view + properties filter) and the refused-merge row are red on semantics;
- "the binding filter scopes the aggregate", "a named saved view's filter scopes the aggregate" and the sort/limit whole-bag row are red on wire shape only. With a binding present, every filter source is now lowered to the ObjectQL AST before merging, as the gate does.

Rows:

1. the dataSource form calls aggregate for the bound object and paints the value;
2. dataSource.object wins over properties.object when both are set;
3. control: the properties form is unchanged;
4. the find() fallback reads the bound object when the adapter cannot aggregate;
5. a binding that names no object supplies nothing, and the flat object stands;
6. one bus event re-reads it, keyed on the resolved object;
7. the key is the binding, not the flat object it outranks;
8. filter: the binding filter scopes the aggregate;
9. filter: properties.filter is AND-combined with the binding filter — both reach the aggregate, neither is dropped;
10. filter: a named view's filter and properties.filter are both applied, AND-combined;
11. filter: a merge the converter refuses reports on the error panel and aggregates nothing;
12. view: a named saved view's filter scopes the aggregate;
13. view: one that cannot be resolved reports and aggregates nothing;
14. view: an unresolvable one does not fall back to properties.object — no object while it is unresolved;
15. sort and limit are not read: the options bag stays whole with a binding and a view carrying both;
16. limit is not read on the find() fallback either: a count is never capped;
17. the registration declares dataSource as an object binding, and object is no longer required;
18. the html tier accepts the dataSource form without a diagnostic (control in the same row: `element:text` still reports `has no prop "dataSource"`).

**Ablations** at 37bc45f74c, through `objectstack/scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` in wrap mode with its trap-armed restore. Each was run over the pin file plus the three pre-existing `element:number` files (`elementNumberFilterMembers-8071`, `elementReaders.invalidationRefetch-10623`, `element-number.contractEnvelope-6726`), 33 rows in all. Each restore printed `ok restored: blob == HEAD (3ab0d9a745a4) and git diff HEAD is empty`.

| # | ablation | red | green |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | resolution line: `(composed?.object ?? props.object)` becomes `(/* ablation-10909 */ props.object)`; blob `3ab0d9a745a4` to `875d8dfa0e4a` | `11 failed \| 22 passed (33)`: rows 1, 2, 4, 6–10, 12, 15 and 16, the dataSource-form rows that reach the resolution line | both controls, the refused-merge and unresolvable-view rows, the two registration rows, and all 15 rows of the three pre-existing files |
| 2 | AND merge: `mergeFilterNodes(own.node, bound.node)` becomes `(/* ablation-10909-and */ bound.node ?? own.node)`, the rule A semantics; blob `3ab0d9a745a4` to `2a9bf06af87c` | `2 failed \| 31 passed (33)`: exactly the two AND rows, 9 and 10 | everything else |
| 3 | guard: `unresolved \|\| filterRefusal ? undefined : ` becomes `/* ablation-10909-guard */ `; blob `3ab0d9a745a4` to `c249c85fa79b` | `2 failed \| 31 passed (33)`: exactly row 11 (refused merge) and row 14 (unresolved view beside a flat object) | everything else |

## Census: element renderers and the `dataSource` binding

Every `element:*` registration is in `@object-ui/components`, and no other package registers one. The census probe rendered each registered element with `dataSource: { object: 'contact' }` and no flat object:

| block | object-bound? | reads `dataSource`? | html tier on `dataSource` |
|---|---|---|---|
| `element:number` | yes (`object`) | **yes** (this PR): `aggregate(contact)` | accepted |
| `element:record_picker` | yes (`object`) | yes: `find(contact)` | accepted |
| `element:repeater` | yes (`object`, required) | no: no read | reports `has no prop "dataSource"` and the missing `object` |
| `element:metadata_viewer` | names a METADATA subject (a state machine's object), not a record query | no | reports `has no prop "dataSource"` |
| `element:text`, `element:divider`, `element:image`, `element:button`, `element:text_input`, `element:definition-list` | no | no | reports `has no prop "dataSource"` |

`element:form` and `element:filter` have `ComponentPropsMap` rows but no objectui renderer. `element:repeater` is not a spec block: it has no `PageComponentType` member and no `ComponentPropsMap` row. Its declaration and its runtime agree, and the html tier reports the key, so this is an observation, not a finding.

## Consumer sweep

The file set is the `git grep` hits for `element:number`, `ElementNumberRenderer`, `elementDataSourceBlock`, `withElementDataSourceInput` and `ELEMENT_DATA_SOURCE_INPUT` in tests, plus:

- the html-tier manifest and html-tier `dataSource` declaration suites;
- the registry-inputs parity suite and the `element-data-source-input-injection` render probe;
- the `record_picker` data-source and malformed-filter pins;
- the suites that render every element renderer generically.

Fix round 1 adds the gate-family filter-merge tests this change reuses: `ElementDataSourceGate.malformedFilter-10789`, `ElementDataSourceGate.test`, core `filter-source-merge.test`, and `ObjectMetric.elementDataSource.test`.

At 37bc45f74c, 34 files, run under the shared verify lock: `Test Files  34 passed (34)` · `Tests  983 passed (983)`.

The full `@object-ui/components` suite ran at 75f027e5c8 (before this round) in three directory runs: 326 collected files, all green. This round changes only `elements.tsx` and its pin file inside that package. Both are covered above by the directories' own `element:number` files and by the sweep.

- **Open PRs**, read through REST before opening: 19 PRs, all file lists (1,867 rows). None touches `packages/components/src/renderers/basic/`, the parity suite or `content/docs/guide/data-source.md`. Positive control: PR objectui#10908's `packages/types/` files match the same grep.

Main moved 20 commits since the base, and none of them touches the renderer, the parity suite, the guide, `useElementDataSource`, `useResolvedFilter`, the gate, the core data-source module, `filter-converter`, `Registry.ts` or `validate.ts`.

## Fix round 1

This responds to the contract review FAIL at 48d755dfe1, on text and one seat ruling. Object resolution, the unchanged properties form, the registration, the census and the pins held.

- **Seat ruling B, filter AND-combine.** Implemented in the renderer with the gate's `toFilterNodeSafely` + `mergeFilterNodes`.
  - The precedence row flipped to assert that both filters reach the aggregate.
  - New rows: a view filter plus `properties.filter`; a refused merge taking the error panel with no aggregate call.
  - The registered `filter` description is the ruling's text verbatim. The guide paragraph and the changeset bullet say AND-combined.
  - `record_picker` is untouched.
- **Changeset:**
  - the frontmatter becomes `minor`;
  - the Clause paragraph is replaced with the review's `Clause-②: yes (widening)` text verbatim;
  - "accepted by both validators" becomes "which the spec lint gate accepts, as `objectui validate` will once objectui#10908 arms the type";
  - the filter bullet now states AND-combine and the loud refusal.
- **PR body:** line 2 is `Clause-②: yes (widening)`.
- **Unresolved-guard pin:** `dataSource: { object: 'contact', view: 'no_such_view' }` beside `properties.object: 'contact'` asserts no aggregate call and the error panel. The guard ablation reddens exactly that row and the refused-merge row.
- **`MEMBER_PINS` prose:** rewritten for rule B. It no longer says the declaration carries "nothing about members"; it says the injected description lists the five members generically and the pin carries which of them this block reads.

## Acceptance notes

- **This unblocks PR objectui#10908.** It is the contract review's option (c) sequencing. With this landed, both validators, the html tier and the renderer tell one story about `{ dataSource: { object } }`, and PR objectui#10908's arm (which accepts `properties.filter` beside a binding filter or view) now matches a renderer that honours both.
- **Clause-②: yes (widening).** The published `element:number` manifest entry declares `dataSource`, and `object` is no longer `required`. The html tier, and the objectstack CLI's JSX gate that reads the manifest, now also accept a node that names neither `object` nor a binding, which paints the empty dash. That case is still reported on the JSON door by the spec lint gate (advisory), and after PR objectui#10908 by its arm when a bag is present. A runtime "no object named" notice, or a one-of check at the html tier, would be a follow-up card. Precedent: objectui#10508 made the same trade on calendar and gantt `objectName`.
- **Wire shape with a binding.** When a binding is present, every filter source is lowered to the ObjectQL AST before it reaches `aggregate()` / `find()`, as `ElementDataSourceGate` does for `object-metric`. Without a binding, `properties.filter` is sent as authored, as before.
- **Studio is unchanged.** Studio's block config for `element:number` stays properties-only and offers no `dataSource` editor.
- **The error-panel title** "could not be resolved" is imprecise for a refused filter; the panel's message names the refused rule. `record_picker` shares the wording. This is a review nit, and the text is unchanged here.
